data.heading: ## viola-0.2.0
requirements: _Capabilities this version delivers, derived from `viola-0.2.0/intent.md` (the intent-file path). Ids are
version-scoped (`v2-NN`), opened at 01 by route's ID rule after 0.1.0's `v1-NN`. Each line carries its finding's
EXPECT; the matching OBSERVED clause travels into the ledger as `observed_gap`. A line that removes or replaces a
built item cites its census rows (`doc:viola-0.2.0/census`); a range `C-a…C-b` names every id between, each a row of
that group, as the intent lists them. The census's `built: no` text rows (intent F-11) are owed no capability: a
0-pending wrap applies them from the card's word._
## (b) What leaves — the census's built rows

title: The fleet: lineage, launch and windows

data.heading: ### Epoch 5 — The fleet: lineage, launch and windows

data.head: Lineage registry — `lineage` event at launch; fleet trees on `list` in its fixed columns, plain when piped; parent kept by `revive`; links drawn apart, name-checked
`viola open` — a terminal window per session beside its parent; closed flag allowlist, no shell; window identity and origin in its own state, logged codes-only
`viola focus` — the session's window raised and its workspace shown through Hyprland, by recorded identity or ancestry; a named refusal otherwise
`viola up` — the fleet re-opened after a reboot, each resumed in place in its workspace, parents first, pid-and-start-verified live ones skipped, logged per instance
`viola adopt` — a plain `claude` session, by session-shaped id, closed and resumed under an operator-given name and parent; the live-elsewhere refusal guards it

Fleet console view — a tiled Hyprland window whole at quarter-screen: lineage trees, each session's state in the board's words, wheel holder, last activity; rows control-escaped
Console actions — every verb by keyboard alone, no key trap, through the CLI verbs; a send shows its readback; refusals as `unable` lines

record.title: The budget gate removed whole

verification.acceptance: An automated send is never refused on budget; no budget reading, budget file, paused state, release option, board field, ledger row or log field remains in the product or its tests; the exit status once used for a budget pause is retired and not reused.

title: Launch a session into the fleet

record.title: Launch a session into the fleet
record.requirement: `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] -- claude …` opens a new terminal window running `viola run <name> …`, placed beside its parent's window (same workspace, next to it) on Hyprland and left to the window manager elsewhere; it returns once the instance is live, records the window's identity, defaults the parent to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` when an agent calls it from its own shell, and logs each open's origin (`cli` · `agent`)
record.observed_gap: viola cannot open a session itself: a wrapped CLI runs only inside a terminal the human already opened, and launching is a 123-line shell script outside the product that places the window by walking the launcher's process ancestry.

verification.acceptance: From the CLI and from an agent's own shell, an open brings up a new terminal window running the named wrapped session, placed beside its parent's window on Hyprland and left to the window manager elsewhere; it returns only once the session is live, records the window's identity and the open's origin, and names the calling agent as the parent when none is given.

data.line: - **v2-07** · Launch a session into the fleet — `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] -- claude …` opens a new terminal window running `viola run <name> …`, placed beside its parent's window (same workspace, next to it) on Hyprland and left to the window manager elsewhere; it returns once the instance is live, records the window's identity, defaults the parent to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME` when an agent calls it from its own shell, and logs each open's origin (`cli` · `agent`) (per intent F-01, ruling 3).

record.title: The launch authority bounded
record.requirement: opening a process passes the wrapped CLI only flags from a closed allowlist, builds no shell line, and quotes nothing through a shell; the argv surface, the allowlist and the agent path stand on a security-plan Decisions Log entry
record.observed_gap: Launching a process is new authority with no decision behind it: no argv quoting rule, flag allowlist or agent path is recorded.

verification.acceptance: An open carrying a flag outside the closed allowlist is refused before anything starts; no shell line is ever built from the given arguments, whatever characters they hold; a security decision entry names the argument surface, the allowlist and the agent path.

data.line: - **v2-08** · The launch authority bounded — opening a process passes the wrapped CLI only flags from a closed allowlist, builds no shell line, and quotes nothing through a shell; the argv surface, the allowlist and the agent path stand on a security-plan Decisions Log entry (per intent F-01).

record.title: The lineage registry

record.observed_gap: viola list is flat and a session's parent is known nowhere; the overseers run unwrapped and show as anonymous read-only rows.

verification.acceptance: A session's declared parent and role are recorded once at launch and read back the same after a crash and a replay; the board shows the fleet as trees; a reused name starts with no parent; a revived session keeps its parent; no parent edge changes the wheel, the links or whether a send is accepted; the overseers run wrapped with their parents declared.

record.title: Focus a session's window
record.requirement: `viola focus <name>` brings that session's window forward and switches to its workspace through Hyprland's own dispatch, by the identity recorded at `open`, or for a hand-started `viola run` by the wrapper's process ancestry; with none found it refuses with a named cause, and outside Hyprland it refuses `unsupported`
record.observed_gap: Finding the right window among about ten is the founder's own search; nothing in viola knows which window a session lives in.

verification.acceptance: Focusing a named session brings its window forward on its workspace on Hyprland, for a session viola opened and for one started by hand; with no window found it refuses with a named cause, and outside Hyprland it refuses as unsupported.

data.line: - **v2-11** · Focus a session's window — `viola focus <name>` brings that session's window forward and switches to its workspace through Hyprland's own dispatch, by the identity recorded at `open`, or for a hand-started `viola run` by the wrapper's process ancestry; with none found it refuses with a named cause, and outside Hyprland it refuses `unsupported` (per intent F-03, ruling 3).

title: A turn ended by an API error ends the turn

record.title: A turn ended by an API error ends the turn
record.requirement: such an end is detected and logged as a turn end with its cause, the instance returns to idle, and the driver can send again with no human `pause` + `release`
record.observed_gap: The Stop hook does not fire on an API-error end, so no turn end is written; send refuses a running turn forever, wait never returns, and only the human's pause and release recover it (V147, claude 2.1.296).

verification.acceptance: A turn ended by an API error is logged as a turn end with its cause, the instance reads idle, and the driver's next send is accepted with no human step; a test fails before the fix.

data.line: - **v2-16** · A turn ended by an API error ends the turn — such an end is detected and logged as a turn end with its cause, the instance returns to idle, and the driver can send again with no human `pause` + `release` (per intent F-06a, V147).

record.title: `wait`'s documented wake condition
record.requirement: `wait` wakes on a documented condition the driver can rely on: a question asked at a turn end that still holds a background task wakes it, and a turn end with no tasks followed at once by a notification gives no false wake
record.observed_gap: wait misses a question asked at a turn end that still holds a background task, which the driver learns of only on its next heartbeat; a task-free turn end followed at once by a notification gives a false wake (V150).

verification.acceptance: A waiting driver is woken by a question asked at a turn end that still holds a background task and is not woken by a notification right after a task-free turn end; the wake condition is documented; each case has a test that fails before the fix.

data.line: - **v2-17** · `wait`'s documented wake condition — `wait` wakes on a documented condition the driver can rely on: a question asked at a turn end that still holds a background task wakes it, and a turn end with no tasks followed at once by a notification gives no false wake (per intent F-06b, V150; 0.1.0 v1-11's log half).

title: A key answering the CLI's session-feedback survey keeps the wheel

record.title: A key answering the CLI's session-feedback survey keeps the wheel
record.requirement: a key that answers a non-editing CLI prompt of a measured grammar does not take the wheel; the session-feedback survey joins the closed non-editing list once its grammar is measured live, and no shape joins it unmeasured

data.head: # Viola 0.2.0 — vision

body:
**Source:** `viola-0.2.0/intent.md` (the intent-file path), reviewed with the founder 2026-11-08, written against
`doc:viola-0.2.0/census` (749 rows, the founder's own word on the card 2026-11-08 19:59:58Z).

data.head: ## The problem this version advances

body:
0.1.0 made one Claude Code session drivable by another (`run · send · wait · last · answer · pause · release ·
revive · verify · list`), and the overseer pair drives its builders through it every day. The fleet around those
sessions is still built by hand, outside the product: shell scripts open and place terminals on Hyprland
(`vstart.sh`), rebuild the layout after a reboot (`up.sh`) and wrap `viola wait` (`pwait.sh`); the overseers run
unwrapped, so the board shows them as anonymous read-only rows; and `viola list` is flat, so nobody can see which
builder belongs to which overseer, or who is working, stalled or waiting on a dialog. Daily driving has measured
failure modes the product leaves to the human.

data.head: ## Who and why

body:
The founder runs about ten sessions at once on his Omarchy host and needs to see and steer them as one fleet from one
place (his headline: «Флот сессий + боли драйвера»). Today that place is a set of shell scripts and his memory.

data.head: ## In

body: - The corrective head: 0.1.0's Epoch 8 cleanup, the dialog-hold ceiling read live, and v1-27 proved.

- What leaves by the census: the budget gate whole and the status-line interception that fed it (the founder,
  2026-11-08: «Убрать совсем»), and the web's one built remnant (the secret scan's `cookie` class).

- The fleet: launching sessions with a declared parent, the lineage registry, window focus and placement through
  Hyprland, restoring the fleet after a reboot, adopting a plain session, and an interactive terminal console tiled
  on Hyprland that reaches every verb.
- Driver reliability: every measured pain point (F-06a–l) closed with a test that fails before the fix.

data.head: ## Out

body: - Any web or graphical UI (the HTTP server, SSE, the browser page and its a11y harness); no node graph of the fleet.
- Windows and macOS entirely (the code stays recoverable at `multi-os-final`).
- An MCP `spawn` tool: agents launch through the CLI verb.

- The window features outside Hyprland: there `open` and `up` open plain terminal windows the window manager places,
  and only `focus` and the placement refuse `unsupported`. The core runs on any current Linux distribution.

data.head: ## What "0.2.0 done" means

body:
On the founder's Omarchy host the pair's whole fleet (overseer1, the project overseers, their builders) is started by
viola, restored by viola after a reboot, and seen and driven from one console; `vstart.sh`, `up.sh` and `pwait.sh` are
retired because nothing calls them; every Driver reliability finding is closed with a test that fails before the fix;
and every ledger capability is `verified` or the founder's `deferred`.

title: Context — the problem this version solves

data.head: ## Context — the problem this version solves

body:
0.1.0 made one Claude Code session drivable by another: `run · send · wait · last · answer · pause · release ·
revive · verify · list`. That works. The overseer pair now drives its builders through the product every day.
The FLEET around those sessions is still built by hand, outside the product:
- `vstart.sh`, 123 lines, opens a terminal and places it on Hyprland by walking the process ancestry.
- `up.sh`, 56 lines, rebuilds the layout after a reboot.
- `pwait.sh` is a waiter wrapped around `viola wait`.
- The overseers themselves run unwrapped, so `viola list` shows them as anonymous read-only uuid rows.

- `viola list` is flat. Nobody can see which builder belongs to which overseer, or which sessions are working,
  stalled, or waiting on a dialog.
And the daily driving has measured failure modes the product leaves to the human (the Driver reliability findings below).

**Core problem:** the founder runs about ten sessions at once and needs to see and steer them as one fleet from one
place. Today that place is a set of shell scripts and the founder's memory.

data.head: ## Definition of done (what "0.2.0 done" means)

body: On the founder's Omarchy host:

- The pair's whole fleet (overseer1, the project overseers, their builders) is started by viola, restored by viola
  after a reboot, and seen and driven from one console.
- `vstart.sh`, `up.sh` and `pwait.sh` are retired, because nothing calls them any more.
- Every Driver reliability finding below is closed, with a test that fails before the fix.

data.head: ## Scope

body: - Launching sessions with a declared parent.
- The lineage registry.
- Window focus and placement through Hyprland.
- Restoring the fleet after a reboot.
- The interactive console.
- Driver reliability.
- Any web or graphical UI: the HTTP server, SSE, the browser page and its a11y harness (the founder's rulings 4 and 6).

- Windows and macOS entirely (ruling 3): no build target, no CI job, no raise or placement branch. Their 0.1.0 code
  is removed before 0.2.0 starts (0.1.0's «Linux-only code and CI»).

- An MCP `spawn` tool: none in 0.2.0; agents launch through the CLI verb (`open-questions.md` Q6 F-e). `adopt` is IN
  (F-07, the founder's word 2026-11-04).

- A node graph of the fleet (the 2026-09-30 idea, the Houdini-style graph of 2026-10-29): no graphical surface in
  0.2.0 (rulings 4 and 6); the console's trees (F-05) are the fleet's view.

data.head: ## Findings (OBSERVED → EXPECT)

title: F-01 · Launch a session into the fleet

data.head: ### F-01 · Launch a session into the fleet

body:
- **OBSERVED:** viola cannot open a session itself. `viola run` wraps a CLI only inside a terminal the human
  already opened. Launching is a 123-line shell script outside the product (`andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/vstart.sh`):
  it uses `xdg-terminal-exec`, a window title, and Hyprland placement by walking the launcher's process ancestry.

- **EXPECT:** `viola open <name> [--parent <name>] [--role overseer|builder|worker] [--cwd <dir>] [--workspace N] --
  claude …` opens a new terminal window on Omarchy running `viola run <name> …`. The window is placed beside its
  parent's (same workspace, next to it). The open returns once the instance is live and records the window's identity.

- An agent can call it from its own shell. The parent then defaults to the caller's `VIOLA_NAME`, and every open
  logs its origin (`cli` · `agent`).

- Launching a process is new authority: a security-plan Decisions Log entry covers the argv quoting surface, the
  closed flag allowlist (`launch.json`, from `deferred-from-0.1.0.md`) and the agent path.

data.head: ### F-02 · The lineage registry

body:
- **OBSERVED:** `viola list` is flat, and a session's parent is known nowhere. The overseers run unwrapped and show
  as `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` uuid rows.

- **EXPECT:** a declared parent and role are recorded once, at launch, in the instance's own event log (Q5 shape
  (ii), a `lineage` event, one writer, replayable). From that:
  - `list` and the console show the fleet as trees.
  - A reused name never inherits an old parent.
  - `revive` keeps the node's parent.
  - A parent edge is a drawing label only. It never changes the wheel, links, or who may `send`.

- Observed `link`s are shown apart from parent edges. A link name is shown only after it parses through
  `ViolaName::try_new`, which absorbs the CARRY `res-ycydja7a`.

data.head: ### F-03 · Focus a session's window

body:
- **OBSERVED:** finding the right window among about ten is the founder's own search. Nothing in viola knows which
  window a session lives in.

- **EXPECT:** `viola focus <name>` brings that session's window forward and switches to its workspace, through
  Hyprland's own dispatch, by the window identity recorded at `open`. For a session started by hand with
  `viola run`, the identity is found from the wrapper's process ancestry. If none is found, the verb refuses with
  a named cause rather than guessing.

title: F-04 · Restore the fleet after a reboot

data.head: ### F-04 · Restore the fleet after a reboot

body:
- **OBSERVED:** after a reboot or a Claude Code update, `up.sh` rebuilds the layout by hand, and the human re-raises
  the builders. Measured 2026-11-02/03: a wrapper restart also lost the budget override the founder had given, so
  the gate closed again (see F-06d).

- **EXPECT:** `viola up` re-opens every instance that was live before the host went down, each resumed in place
  (0.1.0's `revive`), in its recorded workspace and placement, parents before children. It skips any instance
  that is still live, and prints one line per instance.

title: F-05 · The fleet console (the founder's ruling 2)

data.head: ### F-05 · The fleet console (the founder's ruling 2)

body:
- **OBSERVED:** watching and steering the fleet takes several verbs and a lot of `list` reading. Statuses such as
  a pending dialog, the wheel, a budget pause or a stalled turn are spread over columns and event logs.

- **EXPECT:** an interactive terminal console for the fleet, in the spirit of `btop`, keyboard-driven and native to
  the Omarchy look. The founder's word (2026-11-04): it can be tiled into a quarter of the screen to keep it in view,
  never a floating window as `btop` is on Omarchy. So it opens as a TILED Hyprland window, and it stays whole and
  usable at quarter-screen size. It shows:
  - the trees from F-02;
  - each session's state at a glance: working, idle, waiting on a dialog, stalled (no budget state: F-06i);
  - the wheel holder;
  - the last activity.

  From a selected session it reaches every verb viola has: open a child, focus its window, send, answer a pending
  dialog, read the last turn, pause, release, revive. The CLI verbs stay the scriptable surface. The console is a
  view over them, with no second code path for an action.

title: F-06 · Driver reliability (the pain points measured while driving)

data.head: ### F-06 · Driver reliability (the pain points measured while driving)

body:
- **a. A turn ended by an API error leaves the instance stuck** (V147, measured 2026-10-26 on claude 2.1.296).
  - OBSERVED: the Stop hook does not fire on an API-error end, so no `turn-ended` is written. `send` refuses
    `turn-running` forever, `wait` never returns, and the only recovery is the human's `pause` + `release`.
  - EXPECT: such an end is detected and logged as a turn end with its cause. The instance returns to idle and the
    driver can send again.

- **b. `wait` misses a question asked at a turn end that still holds a background task** (V150).
  - OBSERVED: the driver learns of it only on its next heartbeat. The opposite also happens: a turn end with 0
    tasks, followed at once by a notification, gives a false wake.
  - EXPECT: `wait` has a documented wake condition the driver can rely on, covering both cases. `pwait.sh` is then
    unnecessary.

- **c. A skill send whose text ends in a space is read as the human's** (V133).
  - OBSERVED: the CLI trims the space, the echoed prompt no longer matches, the wheel goes to `human`, and the
    send exits 13.
  - EXPECT: the driver's own send is recognised whatever whitespace the CLI trims.

- **d. The budget gate acts on a stale or lost reading** (V152, V156).
  - OBSERVED: the gate held a chunk on a reading more than three days old. The board's BAY line prints
    `budget-paused` while the row is clear. An override was lost across a wrapper restart, and after an account
    switch the gate closed on the previous account's reading.
  - EXPECT: **closed by removal** (F-06i, the founder's ruling 2026-11-08): the gate, its reading and its override no
    longer exist, so nothing can act on a stale or lost reading.

- **e. The 0.1.0 `send` race** (residual `res-vd6nzh42`).
  - OBSERVED: a turn that starts during the readiness gate's wait gets the send typed into it.
  - EXPECT: re-checked after the gate, or the race closed another way. Absorbed.

- **f. A question first raised by PermissionRequest** (residual `res-w2ape2nw`).
  - OBSERVED: it is answered `null` to the human.
  - EXPECT: such a question is answered with a body (PermissionRequest `allow` + `updatedInput` carrying the input
    plus `answers`), through a 15th ledger row, its `viola verify` probe and a re-stamp of the CLI versions.
    **Absorbed** (the founder, 2026-11-08); it needs at least 8 live sessions, the cap given by him on its chunk.

title: F-07 · Adopt a plain session into the fleet (the founder's word, 2026-11-04)

data.head: ### F-07 · Adopt a plain session into the fleet (the founder's word, 2026-11-04)

body:
- **OBSERVED:** a `claude` session started outside viola is a read-only uuid row. It has no name and no parent, and
  no verb reaches it.

- **EXPECT:** `viola adopt --name [--parent

]` closes that session and resumes it under viola, with a name and its place in the fleet. It is built on 0.1.0's `revive`; viola never takes over a running process's terminal. The live-elsewhere refusal guards it. This is how the overseers move under viola.

- **g. A key answering the CLI's own feedback survey takes the wheel** (V158, measured 2026-11-04T21:37Z, claude 2.1.296).
  - OBSERVED: the founder pressed 3 on the CLI's "how is this session" survey, and the product wrote
    `wheel {human, human-input}`. The builder's next question went to the human, not held for the driver.
  - EXPECT: a key that answers a non-editing CLI prompt of a measured grammar does not take the wheel. A shape joins
    the wheel's closed non-editing list only when measured, by its exact grammar, on the founder's word (F-W2).
    **His word given 2026-11-08:** the CLI's session-feedback survey joins the list once its grammar is measured live.

- **h. Product-owned session settings and local commands** (overseer1's relay, 2026-11-06).
  - OBSERVED: dropping MCP servers from a wrapped session needed `/mcp disable …` typed into it (the CLI writes `disabledMcpServers` into `~/.claude.json`), because the product line cannot take a second `--settings`. `viola send` carried each local slash command but exited 13 `not-delivered no-prompt-submitted`: a local command submits no prompt, so a send that ran reads as failed.
  - EXPECT: the product writes such keys into its own settings for the sessions it launches, and `send` recognises a local command's own echo (`<local-command-stdout>`) as delivery.

- **i. The budget governor's source (the founder's question, 2026-11-06 20:53Z).**
  - OBSERVED: the gate reads `rate_limits` from the CLI's status-line payload, which viola intercepts on its way to the user's own status-line command. The `statusline-rate-limits` ledger row demands both windows, so `viola verify` reads red on an account whose payload carries only the seven-day window (2026-11-06: 23/24). That left v1-27 unproved and deferred. The gate also closed on stale or lost readings (V152, V156). The founder: «это мой чистый инструмент … почему Viola в принципе на него ориентируется».
  - **RULED 2026-11-08 by the founder, «Убрать совсем»:** viola reads no rate limits and gates nothing on budget;
    the budget is the founder's own instrument.
  - EXPECT: the budget gate is removed whole — the `rate_limits` reading and `~/.viola/budget.json`, the gate on
    automated `send`, `viola release --budget`, the `budget-paused` state and the board's budget fields, the
    `statusline-rate-limits` ledger row, and the status-line interception that existed only to feed the reading (the
    user's own status-line command runs as if viola were not there). The masters' budget passages and the
    capabilities that assert the gate are retired through route's census. With the row gone, v1-27 is proved early.

- **j. An MCP call can outlast the client's tool-call timeout** (0.1.0's deferred v1-21, its last clause).
  - OBSERVED: the client's default timeout is unmeasured (known only to exceed 50 s: a `wait` answered at 50 012 ms
    on 2.1.287), and a `send`'s longest block is 48.5 s plus the paste, which no bound caps.
  - EXPECT: the client's timeout is measured, and every MCP call is bounded below it, with a test.

- **k. The ledger's two owed rows** (0.1.0's deferred v1-34): the harness-prefix row (the prefix the CLI puts on a
  message another session sends in) and the R8 identity-floor row (which `CLAUDE*` environment names a wrapped child
  keeps). The fleet makes cross-session sends daily traffic, so the first row is now load-bearing.
  **In 0.2.0, the founder's word 2026-11-08**, which also rules the two probes: a second session sending into a
  `viola verify` child, and the capture reading environment variable NAMES (never values). Live sessions on the
  chunk's cap.
